subject: humanities
passage: Qawwali, a form of devotional music performed across Pakistan and northern India, is traditionally flexible in length. At a live gathering, singers may repeat and extend a single line many times in response to the mood of the listeners, so one song can last half an hour or more. When qawwali was first recorded in the early 1900s, however, each side of a gramophone disc could hold only about three minutes of sound. Because of this limit, early qawwali recordings most likely ______
stem: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: captured the full length of typical qawwali performances at live gatherings.
choices.B: replaced traditional qawwali songs with entirely new compositions for discs.
choices.C: caused qawwali singers to stop repeating lines in their live performances.
choices.D: offered shortened versions of songs that ran far longer when performed live.

explanation.why: Live qawwali songs can last half an hour or more, but a disc side held only about three minutes. To fit on a disc, recorded songs would have had to be much shorter than live versions.
explanation.A: Incorrect. A three-minute side could not hold a performance lasting half an hour or more.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text gives no evidence that recordings used new songs; the time limit points to shortening, not replacing.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text describes a limit on recordings; it gives no evidence that live performances changed.
explanation.D: Correct. A three-minute disc side could hold only a small part of a song that might last thirty minutes live.
